record.title: The Markoff graph connectivity conjecture modulo primes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be the set of positive integer solutions to

$$
x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz,
$$

and let $\mathcal M_p$ be the set of non-zero solutions modulo a prime $p$. The functional graph is generated by the involutions

$$
\mathcal R_1(x,y,z)=(3yz-x,y,z),
$$

and the analogous maps $\mathcal R_2,\mathcal R_3$, together with permutations of the coordinates. Let $\mathcal C_p\subseteq\mathcal M_p$ denote the largest connected component of the resulting graph. **Baragar–Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak conjecture.** For every prime $p$, one has

$$
\mathcal C_p=\mathcal M_p.
$$
 This asserts that the Markoff triples generate all non-zero solutions modulo $p$ and that the associated functional graph is connected; the supplied text gives no evidence resolving the conjecture.
record.source_name: Sergei V. Konyagin, Igor E. Shparlinski and Ilya V. Vyugin, “Polynomial Equations in Subgroups and Applications”, arXiv:2005.05315 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.05315

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

record.title: The Fermat Deligne-period quotient conjecture
record.statement:
Assume the sub-Hodge-structure splitting conjecture, and let $\mathbf{H}^n_{a,j}$ be a two-dimensional direct summand in the resulting split, defined over the smallest real algebraic number field $k$. Let $c^{+}(\mathbf{H}^n_{a,j})$ and $c^{-}(\mathbf{H}^n_{a,j})$ denote its Deligne periods. **Deligne-period quotient conjecture.** These periods are well defined up to multiplication by nonzero elements of $k$, and

$$
\frac{c^+(\mathbf{H}^n_{a,j})}{c^-(\mathbf{H}^n_{a,j})}=\sigma i,
$$

where $\sigma$ is a real algebraic number. Assuming additionally the mirror-map conjecture, $\sigma$ belongs to the real field $\mathbb{Q}(\xi)$. Numerical computations for the two-dimensional summands with $n=3,4,6,8,10$ support algebraicity of the quotient, but the stated general claim remains unproved.
record.source_name: Wenzhe Yang, “Rank-2 attractors and Fermat type CY n-folds”, arXiv:2005.06722 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.06722

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

record.title: Martin and Thatte's maximum agreement subtree conjecture for balanced trees
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal S}$ and ${\mathcal T}$ be balanced rooted binary phylogenetic $X$-trees, meaning that each has $2^m$ leaves for some non-negative integer $m$ and height $m$, and let $n=|X|$. Write ${\rm mast}({\mathcal S},{\mathcal T})$ for the maximum size of a common restriction that is an agreement subtree of ${\mathcal S}$ and ${\mathcal T}$. **Martin and Thatte's conjecture.**

$$
{\rm mast}({\mathcal S},{\mathcal T})\geq n^{\frac12}.
$$

The conjecture proposed a square-root lower bound for the size of a maximum agreement subtree of two balanced rooted binary phylogenetic trees. It is refuted by the paper's main theorem, which gives, for every $c>0$, balanced rooted binary trees with maximum agreement subtree of size less than $c n^{\frac12}$; hence the conjecture is false.
record.source_name: Magnus Bordewich, Simone Linz, Megan Owen, Katherine St. John, Charles Semple and Kristina Wicke, “On the maximum agreement subtree conjecture for balanced trees”, arXiv:2005.07357 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.07357

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Rejmer's conjecture on the indefinite continuation of his coloring algorithm
record.statement: Let $c(1)=+1$ and construct a perfectly balanced multiplicative coloring recursively by the greedy procedure described in the paper: at each step color the next integer while preserving perfect balance and multiplicativity, switching an earlier prime when necessary. **Rejmer's conjecture.** Rejmer's algorithm runs ad infinitum. Computational experiments produce perfectly balanced multiplicative colorings through $10^9$ steps, but it is not known whether the procedure can always continue indefinitely.
record.source_name: Bartłomiej Bosek and Jarosław Grytczuk, “Reflections on the Erdős Discrepancy Problem”, arXiv:2005.14283 (2020).

record.title: The rank-one projection conjecture at the exceptional parameter
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$ be an integer, let $|x\rangle$ be a vector on the unit sphere in $\mathbf R^{d-1}$, and construct matrices $A_m$ using $V_m=2|x\rangle\langle x|-I_{d-1}$ for every $m$. **Rank-one projection conjecture.** For every $d\geq 3$, there exists such a vector $|x\rangle$ for which the set

$$
\{A_mA_n\}
$$

is linearly independent when $t=-\frac{1}{d-1}$. This concerns the exceptional parameter where the highly symmetric choice of projection vector produces a degeneracy.
record.source_name: Uffe Haagerup, Magdalena Musat and Mary Beth Ruskai, “Extreme Points and Factorizability for New Classes of Unital Quantum Channels”, arXiv:2006.03414 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.03414

record.title: Esperet–Kang–Thomassé conjecture on dense induced bipartite subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive real number, and let $G$ be a triangle-free graph with minimum degree at least $d$. An **induced bipartite subgraph** of $G$ is a bipartite subgraph induced by a subset of the vertices of $G$, and its average degree is the average of its vertex degrees. **Esperet–Kang–Thomassé conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains an induced bipartite subgraph with average degree

$$
\Omega(\ln d).
$$

This conjecture strengthens the known bound of order $\ln d/\ln\ln d$ proved for every triangle-free graph of minimum degree $d$. It asks whether the logarithmic factor can be achieved without the additional $\ln\ln d$ loss.
record.source_name: Stefan Glock, “A note on dense bipartite induced subgraphs”, arXiv:2006.05101 (2020).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1811.11116](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.11116), [arXiv:1810.12144](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.12144), [arXiv:1808.02512](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02512).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05101

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

record.title: Grzesik–Janzer–Nagy conjecture on Turán numbers of graph blow-ups
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a graph, and let $F[r]$ denote its $r$-blow-up, obtained by replacing each vertex of $F$ with an independent set of size $r$ and each edge with a copy of $K_{r,r}$. Let $\mathrm{ex}(n,F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $F$-free graph on $n$ vertices.

**Grzesik–Janzer–Nagy conjecture.** If

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,F)=O(n^{2-\alpha})
$$

for some constant $0\leq\alpha\leq1$, then for every positive integer $r$,

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,F[r])=O\left(n^{2-\frac{\alpha}{r}}\right).
$$

The conjecture is known when $F$ is a tree and when $F=K_{s,t}$ with $\alpha=1/s$, including the case $C_4=K_{2,2}$, but it remains open already for even cycles $F=C_{2k}$ with $k\geq3$.
record.source_name: Oliver Janzer, Abhishek Methuku and Zoltán Lóránt Nagy, “On the Turán number of the blow-up of the hexagon”, arXiv:2006.05897 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05897

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2020). “This covers the case $C_4=K_{2,2}$, but already when $F=C_{2k}$ for some $k\geq 3$, the conjecture is open.”

record.title: Weakly supercritical circumference conjecture for random planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of planar graphs, let $P=P(n,m)\in_R\mathcal P(n,m)$ be chosen uniformly at random, and let $L_1=L_1(P)$ be the largest component of $P$. Assume that

$$
m=n/2+s,
$$

where $s=s(n)=o(n)$ and $s^3n^{-2}\to\infty$. The **circumference** $c(L_1)$ is the length of the longest cycle in $L_1$.

**Weakly supercritical circumference conjecture.**

$$
c(L_1)=\Theta_p\left(sn^{-1/3}\right).
$$

This would sharpen the available lower and upper bounds for the circumference of the largest component in the weakly supercritical regime. The statement is presented as a consequence of the conjectured linear circumference of random cubic planar multigraphs.
record.source_name: Mihyun Kang and Michael Missethan, “Longest and shortest cycles in random planar graphs”, arXiv:2006.09697 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.09697

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

record.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficient maximality conjecture for uniform matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $d$ on $m+d$ elements, and write its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial as

$$
P_M(t)=\sum_i c^i t^i.
$$

Let $U_{m,d}$ denote the uniform matroid of rank $d$ on $m+d$ elements, and let $c^i_{m,d}(\emptyset)$ be the $i$-th coefficient of its Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial. **Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficient maximality conjecture.** For every such matroid $M$ and every coefficient index $i$,

$$
c^i\leq c^i_{m,d}(\emptyset).
$$

Equivalently, among matroids with rank $d$ and ground-set size $m+d$, the uniform matroid has the largest Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficients. The paper proves this conjecture for sparse paving matroids, but the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: Kyungyong Lee, George D. Nasr and Jamie Radcliffe, “A Combinatorial Formula for Kazhdan-Lusztig Polynomials of Sparse Paving Matroids”, arXiv:2006.10209 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.10209

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

record.title: Berkovich–Uncu's eventual partition inequality for $C^{*}_{L,s}$ and $D_{L,s}$
record.statement:
For positive integers $L$ and $s$ with $L\geq s+1$, let $C^{*}_{L,s}$ be the set of partitions whose smallest part is $s$, whose parts are at most $L+s$, and in which $L$ does not occur. Let $D_{L,s}$ be the set of nonempty partitions with parts in $\{s+1,\ldots,L+s\}$. **Berkovich and Uncu's conjecture.** For positive integers $L\geq 3$ and $s$, there exists an $M$ depending only on $s$ such that

$$
\left|\{\pi\in C^{*}_{L,s}:|\pi|=N\}\right|\geq\left|\{\pi\in D_{L,s}:|\pi|=N\}\right|
$$

for every $N\geq M$. The source presents this as one of several related conjectures and notes that recent progress is discussed later in the paper; its resolution is not established by the supplied context.
record.source_name: Damanvir Singh Binner and Amarpreet Rattan, “On Conjectures Concerning the Smallest Part and Missing Parts of Integer Partitions”, arXiv:2006.15287 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15287

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

record.title: Berkovich–Uncu's corrected nonnegativity conjecture for $G_{L,2}(q)$
record.statement:
For a positive integer $L$, let $G_{L,2}(q)$ be the difference of the generating series for partitions with smallest part $2$ and largest-minus-smallest part at most $L$, and for partitions with smallest part at least $3$ and largest-minus-smallest part at most $L$. Write $S\succeq 0$ when every coefficient of the series $S$ is nonnegative. **Berkovich and Uncu's conjecture.**

$$
L=3\implies G_{L,2}(q)+q^3+q^9+q^{15}\succeq 0;
$$

$$
L=4\implies G_{L,2}(q)+q^3+q^9\succeq 0;
$$

$$
L\geq 5\implies G_{L,2}(q)+q^3\succeq 0.
$$

The source explicitly says that it proves this conjecture in the paper, so the claim is solved.
record.source_name: Damanvir Singh Binner and Amarpreet Rattan, “On Conjectures Concerning the Smallest Part and Missing Parts of Integer Partitions”, arXiv:2006.15287 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15287

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The primorial Jacobsthal lower-bound conjecture for missing differences
record.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k>1$. Write $h(k-1)$ for the primorial Jacobsthal function at $k-1$, and let $N_{min}(k)$ be the minimum even positive integer that does not occur as a difference between consecutive integers coprime to the primorial $p_k\#$. **Primorial difference conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k>1$, 

$$
h(k-1)\le N_{min}(k).
$$

This is an empirical assumption supported by all computed cases in the paper, but the cited data do not establish it in general; its status is therefore open.
record.source_name: Mario Ziller, “On differences between consecutive numbers coprime to primorials”, arXiv:2007.01808 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.01808

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

record.title: The approximate packing conjecture for Hamilton cycles in random hypercube subgraphs
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{Q}^n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, let $\mathcal{Q}^n_p$ be its random subgraph obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$, and let $\delta(\mathcal{Q}^n_p)$ denote its minimum degree. For every $p\in(1/2,1]$ and every $\eta>0$, the **approximate Hamilton-cycle packing conjecture.** Asymptotically almost surely, $\mathcal{Q}^n_p$ contains $(1/2-\eta)\delta(\mathcal{Q}^n_p)$ pairwise edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. This is proposed as an approximate analogue in the hypercube of known packing results for random graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Padraig Condon, Alberto Espuny Díaz, António Girão, Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Hamiltonicity of random subgraphs of the hypercube”, arXiv:2007.02891 (2022).

record.title: Integrality conjecture for ordered multi-degree contributions
record.statement:
Let $(d_0,d_1,d_2)$ be an ordered multi-degree, and let $\operatorname{C}_{\operatorname{ord}}(d_0,d_1,d_2)$ denote its ordered multi-degree contribution. Write $\operatorname{gcd}(d_0,d_1,d_2)$ for the greatest common divisor of the three degrees.

**Integrality conjecture.** The ordered multi-degree contributions satisfy

$$
\operatorname{gcd}(d_0,d_1,d_2)^2\cdot\operatorname{C}_{\operatorname{ord}}(d_0,d_1,d_2)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}.
$$

This predicts a divisibility and nonnegativity property for all ordered multi-degree contributions. The supplied text gives no resolution or further evidence sufficient to determine whether it is known, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Lawrence Jack Barrott and Navid Nabijou, “Tangent curves to degenerating hypersurfaces”, arXiv:2007.05016 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.05016

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2020). “After taking the logarithm, is the coefficient of the diagonal term of the $3$-Kronecker quiver (according to a conjecture of Gross, proved by Reineke ).”

record.title: Even-path inverse Turán conjecture
record.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer, let $P_{2t}$ denote the path of length $2t$, and let $\operatorname{ex}^{-1}(k,H)$ denote the inverse Turán number of $H$, namely the maximum number of edges in a graph whose every $H$-free subgraph has fewer than $k$ edges. A complete $t$-partite graph is **balanced** when its $t$ vertex classes have equal sizes. **Even-path inverse Turán conjecture.** The inverse Turán number of a path of length $2t$ is attained asymptotically by a balanced, complete $t$-partite graph. Therefore, for every $t$, 

$$
\operatorname{ex}^{-1}(k,P_{2t})=\frac{k^2}{2(t-1)^2}\left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right)+o(k^2).
$$

This conjecture identifies balanced complete multipartite graphs as asymptotically extremal for even paths; the source presents it as an open question.
record.source_name: Ervin Győri, Nika Salia, Casey Tompkins and Oscar Zamora, “Inverse Turán numbers”, arXiv:2007.07042 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.07042

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

record.title: Conjecture on recurrence divisibility for algebraic integers
record.statement:
Let $alpha \in \bar{\Z}$, let $K=\Q(\alpha)$, and let $d_k(\alpha)$ denote the largest positive integer such that

$$
\alpha^k-1\in d_k(\alpha)\mathcal O_K.
$$

Assume that either (a) $[\Q(\alpha^r):\Q]\geq 3$ for every $r\geq 1$, or (b) $[\Q(\alpha^r):\Q]\geq 2$ for every $r\geq 1$ and $N_K(\alpha)\ne\pm1$. **Conjecture 9.** Under these assumptions, the set

$$
\{k\geq 1\mid d_k(\alpha)=d_1(\alpha)\}
$$

is infinite. The conjecture predicts infinitely many indices at which the divisibility sequence attached to $alpha$ returns to its initial value, outside the exceptional low-degree or quadratic-unit cases discussed in the paper.
record.source_name: Elisa Bellah, “Norm Form Equations and Linear Divisibility Sequences”, arXiv:2007.07392 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.07392

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

record.title: Regular main branches in minimum weighted Szeged index trees
record.statement: Let a **regular ending branch** be a minimal weighted-Szeged-index ending branch whose children have the same order, and let a **main ending branch** be an ending branch directly connected to the root of the tree. **Regular-branch conjecture.** In a minimum weighted Szeged index tree, all but at most one main ending branch are regular ending branches. The conjecture is based on observations of the first 80 minimal ending branches; the paper leaves this structural property open.
record.source_name: Pavol Hell, César Hernández-Cruz and Seyyed Aliasghar Hosseini, “Minimum Weighted Szeged Index Trees”, arXiv:2007.10510 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.10510

record.title: Minimum-degree Oberwolfach conjecture
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a $2$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, and let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, where $d$ is even. An **$F$-decomposition** partitions the edges of $G$ into edge-disjoint copies of $F$.

**Minimum-degree Oberwolfach conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, the following holds for sufficiently large $n$: if

$$
d\ge (3/4+\varepsilon)n,
$$

then $G$ has an $F$-decomposition.

The threshold is motivated by the triangle-factor case, while Hamilton cycles can be decomposed at a lower threshold. The source attributes the conjecture to Glock, Joos, Kühn, Kim, and Osthus and leaves it open.
record.source_name: Stefan Glock, Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Extremal aspects of graph and hypergraph decomposition problems”, arXiv:2008.00926 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00926

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: Minimum-degree Baranyai factorization conjecture
record.statement:
Fix $k$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum vertex degree. A **perfect matching** is a set of pairwise disjoint edges covering all vertices; a decomposition into perfect matchings is a $1$-factorization.

**Minimum-degree Baranyai conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, an $n$-vertex $k$-graph $G$ with

$$
\delta(G)\ge (1/2+\varepsilon)n
$$

can be decomposed into perfect matchings if and only if $k\mid n$ and $G$ is vertex-regular.

This proposes a dense minimum-degree extension of Baranyai's theorem. The divisibility and regularity conditions are necessary, and the source presents sufficiency as open.
record.source_name: Stefan Glock, Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Extremal aspects of graph and hypergraph decomposition problems”, arXiv:2008.00926 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00926

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: Exact high-girth triangle-decomposition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K_3$-divisibility mean that the number of edges is divisible by $3$ and every vertex degree is even. A triangle decomposition of a graph partitions its edges into copies of $K_3$, and its **girth** is the smallest size of a vertex set spanning at least two fewer triangles than vertices.

**High-girth triangle-decomposition conjecture.** For every fixed $g$, every sufficiently large $K_3$-divisible complete graph $K_n$ has a $K_3$-decomposition with girth at least $g$.

This is the quantified exact form of the high-girth Steiner triple system conjecture. The source reports that only the first nontrivial case is known exactly, while approximate results are available for all fixed $g$.
record.source_name: Stefan Glock, Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Extremal aspects of graph and hypergraph decomposition problems”, arXiv:2008.00926 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00926

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: High-girth Nash-Williams conjecture for triangle decompositions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $|G|$ vertices. It is **$K_3$-divisible** if its number of edges is divisible by $3$ and every vertex degree is even. A triangle decomposition with **girth at least $g$** is a partition of the edges into triangles such that no set of fewer than $g$ vertices spans at least two fewer triangles than vertices.

**High-girth Nash-Williams conjecture.** For every fixed $g$, every sufficiently large $K_3$-divisible graph $G$ with

$$
\delta(G)\ge 3|G|/4
$$

has a $K_3$-decomposition with girth at least $g$.

This combines the minimum-degree triangle-decomposition conjecture with Erdős's local-sparsity requirement. The source presents it as a proposed combination of two unresolved conjectures.
record.source_name: Stefan Glock, Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Extremal aspects of graph and hypergraph decomposition problems”, arXiv:2008.00926 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.00926

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: The diagonal-maximality conjecture for inverse Vandermonde matrices
record.statement:
Let $b>1$, and set

$$
n_0=\left\lceil\log_b\left(1+\frac{1}{b}\right)\right\rceil.
$$
 For each $n$, let $M_b(n)$ denote the largest absolute value of an entry of the inverse Vandermonde matrix, and let $c_{i,j,n}$ denote its entries. **Diagonal-maximality conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, there is some $i$ with $0\leq i\leq n_0$ such that

$$
M_b(n)=|c_{i,i,n}|.
$$
 The preceding results show that the limit of $M_b(n)$ is attained asymptotically among finitely many entries, but do not establish that a diagonal entry is maximal for every sufficiently large $n$; this is the remaining unproved assertion.
record.source_name: Carlo Sanna, Jeffrey Shallit and Shun Zhang, “The Largest Entry in the Inverse of a Vandermonde Matrix”, arXiv:2008.01012 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01012

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: A quadratic-degree bound for minimal Ramsey graphs for cliques
record.statement:
Let $s_r(K_k)$ denote the minimum number of edges in an $r$-Ramsey-minimal graph for the clique $K_k$. **Quadratic-degree bound conjecture.** For all $r\geqslant 2$ and $k\geqslant 2$, there exist a constant $C>0$ and a constant-degree polynomial function $f$ such that

$$
s_r(K_k) \leqslant C k^2 r^2 f(\ln k,\ln r).
$$

The conjecture asks for a substantially stronger bound than the preceding polynomial upper bounds, reducing the main dependence on $k$ and $r$ to quadratic factors up to polylogarithmic terms. The source does not indicate that this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: John Bamberg, Anurag Bishnoi and Thomas Lesgourgues, “The minimum degree of minimal Ramsey graphs for cliques”, arXiv:2008.02474 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02474

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: List Colouring Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of maximum degree $\Delta$. Let $E(G)$ denote its edge set, and let $L$ be a list assignment assigning a set of colours $L(e)$ to each edge $e$ of $G$. An **$L$-colouring** is a proper edge-colouring in which the colour assigned to each edge $e$ belongs to $L(e)$.

**List Colouring Conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ and $L$ is a list assignment to $E(G)$ such that

$$
|L(e)|\geq \Delta+1
$$

for every edge $e$ of $G$, then there exists an $L$-colouring of the edges of $G$.

This is the edge-colouring list analogue of the chromatic index bound, and the paper describes it as a conjecture connected to linear arboricity. The supplied text gives no resolution status for this conjecture.
record.source_name: Richard Lang and Luke Postle, “An Improved Bound for the Linear Arboricity Conjecture”, arXiv:2008.04251 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.04251

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: The trimmed exponential Galois group conjecture
record.statement:
For integers $m>n\geq 1$, define the trimmed exponential polynomial

$$
f_{n,m}(x)=\sum_{j=n}^{m}\frac{x^{j-n}}{j!}.
$$

Its degree is $m-n$, and let $G_{f_{n,m}}$ denote its Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$.

**Trimmed exponential Galois group conjecture.** For every $m>n\geq 1$, the polynomial $f_{n,m}$ is irreducible and

$$
G_{f_{n,m}}=S_{m-n}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that trimmed exponentials have the largest possible Galois group, together with irreducibility, and remains open in the stated generality.
record.source_name: Lior Bary-Soroker and Or Ben-Porath, “On the Galois Theory of Generalized Laguerre Polynomials and Trimmed Exponential”, arXiv:2008.05165 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.05165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: Zhang's equitable list arboricity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $L$ be a $k$-assignment for $G$, and call $G$ **equitably $k$-list arborable** if there is an arborable $L$-coloring in which every color class has size at most $\lceil |V(G)|/k\rceil$ for every such $L$. Write $\Delta(G)$ for the maximum degree of $G$.

**Zhang's conjecture.** Any graph $G$ is equitably $k$-list arborable for each $k$ satisfying

$$
k\geq \left\lceil\frac{\Delta(G)+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture is a list analogue of the Equitable Vertex Arboricity Conjecture. It has been verified for 2-degenerate graphs, 3-degenerate claw-free graphs with maximum degree at least $4$, planar graphs with maximum degree at least $8$, and grids of dimensions $2$, $3$, and $4$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Hemanshu Kaul, Jeffrey A. Mudrock and Michael J. Pelsmajer, “On Equitable List Arboricity of Graphs”, arXiv:2008.08926 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1809.08281](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08281).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08926

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020). “Their conjecture is still open and is known as the Equitable $\Delta$-Coloring Conjecture.”

record.title: The quadratic Mader-number conjecture for bioriented cliques
record.statement:
Let $\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_n$ denote the bioriented complete digraph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(F)$ be the smallest integer $k\ge1$ such that every digraph of dichromatic number at least $k$ contains a subdivision of $F$. **The quadratic Mader-number conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_n)\le cn^2
$$

for every positive integer $n$. The conjecture proposes a quadratic upper bound, improving substantially on the paper's general exponential upper bound; it remains open for general digraphs.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Dichromatic number and forced subdivisions”, arXiv:2008.09888 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09888

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020). “While the cases $k=5,6$ of Haj\'{o}s' conjecture remain open, it was disproved for all values $k \ge 7$ by Catlin , who constructed explicit counterexamples, i.e.”

record.title: Long-subdivision extraction conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
For a digraph $D$, write $\delta^+(D)$ for its minimum out-degree. A subdivision-path is a directed path replacing an arc in a subdivision.

**Long-subdivision extraction conjecture.** There is a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and every digraph $D$ with

$$
\delta^+(D)\geq f(k),
$$

there exists a digraph $D'$ with $\delta^+(D')\geq k$ such that $D$ contains a subdivision of $D'$ in which every subdivision-path has length at least two.

The statement would imply the preceding subdivision-preservation conjecture, but is itself unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Oriented cycles in digraphs of large outdegree”, arXiv:2008.13224 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13224

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: In-dominating-set conjecture for digraphs of large outdegree
record.statement:
For a digraph $D$, let $\delta^+(D)$ be its minimum out-degree. A set $X\subseteq V(D)$ is **in-dominating** if every vertex in $V(D)\setminus X$ has an out-neighbor in $X$.

**In-dominating-set conjecture.** There exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $k\geq1$, if

$$
\delta^+(D)\geq f(k),
$$

then there is an in-dominating set $X\subsetneq V(D)$ satisfying $\delta^+(D-X)\geq k$.

The source presents this as a natural statement that would imply the out-leaf extension conjecture; its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Oriented cycles in digraphs of large outdegree”, arXiv:2008.13224 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13224

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: Prime realization conjecture for exceptional harmonic-sum values
record.statement: For a prime $p$, let condition (4.1) be the harmonic-sum congruence defined in the paper, and count the integers $d$ with $d\leq p-1$ for which that condition is not satisfied. **Prime realization conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 1$, there is a prime number $P_k$ such that condition (4.1) does not hold for exactly $k$ values of $d\leq P_k-1$. Numerical computations find such primes for $k\leq 8$, but the general assertion is refuted.
record.source_name: Karl Dilcher and Maciej Ulas, “Divisibility and Arithmetic Properties of a Class of Sparse Polynomials”, arXiv:2008.13475 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13475

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2020). “Let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. Then there is a prime number $P_{k}$ such that does not hold for exactly $k$ values of $d\leq P_{k}-1$.”

record.title: Conjectures for maximum intersection density by permutation-group degree
record.statement:
Let $I(n)$ denote the maximum intersection density among transitive permutation groups of degree $n$. For a transitive group $G$ of degree $n$, let $\Gamma_G$ be its derangement graph.

**Conjectures for $I(n)$.**
1. If $n$ is even but not a power of $2$, then there is a transitive group $G$ of degree $n$ such that $\Gamma_G$ is a complete multipartite graph with $n/2$ parts.
2. If $n$ is a prime power, then $I(n)=1$.
3. If $n=pq$ where $p$ and $q$ are odd primes, then $I(n)=1$.
4. If $n=2q$ where $q$ is prime, then $I(n)=2$.

These conjectures are based on computational evidence for transitive groups of degree at most $48$. The source presents them as conjectural values and constructions for the maximum intersection density.
record.source_name: Andriaherimanana Sarobidy Razafimahatratra, Karen Meagher and Pablo Spiga, “On triangles in derangement graphs”, arXiv:2009.01086 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.01086

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

record.title: Relative Turán lower-bound conjecture for graph hosts
record.statement:
Let $F$ and $H$ be graphs, let $H$ have maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\operatorname{ex}(H,F)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $F$-free subgraph of $H$. **Relative Turán lower-bound conjecture.** As $\Delta\to\infty$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}(H,F)=\Omega\left(\frac{\operatorname{ex}(\Delta,F)}{\Delta^2}\right)e(H).
$$

This is presented as a central consequence of the minimum-degree conjecture above and is expected to hold uniformly for graph hosts of maximum degree $\Delta$. The source describes it as open.
record.source_name: Sam Spiro and Jacques Verstraëte, “Relative Turán Problems for Uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:2009.02416 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02416

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2020). “The main open question for relative Tur\'{a}n numbers of $r$-graphs is to give bounds on $\ex(H,F)$ when $F$ is $r$-partite.”

record.title: Conjecture that every 3-connected graph is s_q-abundant
record.statement: Let $q\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $H$ be a graph. A graph $H$ is **$s_q$-abundant** if there are minimal $q$-Ramsey graphs for $H$ containing arbitrarily many vertices of degree $s_q(H)$, where $s_q(H)$ is the minimum degree that can occur in a minimal $q$-Ramsey graph for $H$. **The 3-connected abundance conjecture.** Every $3$-connected graph $H$ is $s_q$-abundant for any integer $q\geq 2$. The paper proves sufficient conditions for $s_q$-abundance of certain $3$-connected graphs, but leaves the assertion for all $3$-connected graphs as an open problem.
record.source_name: Simona Boyadzhiyska, Dennis Clemens and Pranshu Gupta, “Minimal Ramsey graphs with many vertices of small degree”, arXiv:2009.04159 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.04159

record.title: The two-colour proper-walk connection conjecture for Hamiltonian digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a Hamiltonian digraph, and let $d_D^+(v)$ and $d_D^-(v)$ denote the out-degree and in-degree of a vertex $v\in V(D)$, respectively. A vertex-colouring of $D$ is properly connected by walks when every ordered pair of vertices is joined by a properly coloured directed walk, and let $\overrightarrow{wc}(D)$ be the minimum number of colours in such a colouring. **Two-colour proper-walk connection conjecture.** If

$$
d_D^+(v)\ge 2\quad\text{and}\quad d_D^-(v)\ge 2
$$

for every vertex $v\in V(D)$, then

$$
\overrightarrow{wc}(D)\le 2.
$$

The conjecture removes the preceding restriction that every chord of a Hamiltonian cycle has length at most $\lceil |V(D)|/2\rceil$, and would establish a universal two-colour bound for this class of digraphs.
record.source_name: Anna Fiedorowicz, Elżbieta Sidorowicz and Èric Sopena, “Proper connection and proper-walk connection of digraphs”, arXiv:2009.06331 (2020).

record.title: Li–Horacek–Luo–Miao's planar girth-five list star chromatic index conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least $5$, and let $\Delta$ be its maximum degree. The **list star chromatic index** $ch'_{st}(G)$ is the least list size guaranteeing a star edge-coloring from every assignment of lists of that size.

**Li–Horacek–Luo–Miao's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
ch'_{st}(G)\leq\frac{3}{2}\Delta+c.
$$

For planar graphs of girth $4$, the survey gives examples with $ch'_{st}(G)\geq\frac{13}{8}\Delta-\frac34$, while existing results give upper bounds of the conjectured linear form for sufficiently large girth. The girth-at-least-five case remains open.
record.source_name: Hui Lei and Yongtang Shi, “A survey on star edge-coloring of graphs”, arXiv:2009.08017 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.08017

record.title: Holub–Lužar–Mihaliková–Mockovčiaková–Soták's path–cycle product conjecture
record.statement:
For integers $m\geq2$ and $n\geq3$, let $P_m$ be the path on $m$ vertices, let $C_n$ be the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $P_m\square C_n$ denote their Cartesian product.

**Holub–Lužar–Mihaliková–Mockovčiaková–Soták's conjecture.** There exist constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ such that for all integers $m\geq c_1$ and $n\geq c_2$,

$$
\chi'_{st}(P_m\square C_n)=6.
$$

Known results in the survey determine many cases and leave the range $m\geq7$, $n\geq11$, with $n$ not divisible by $2$ or $3$, unresolved. The conjecture predicts that sufficiently large products in both dimensions have star chromatic index exactly $6$.
record.source_name: Hui Lei and Yongtang Shi, “A survey on star edge-coloring of graphs”, arXiv:2009.08017 (2020).

record.title: Degenerate-graph density conjecture
record.statement:
For $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$, let $\mathcal{D}_k$ be the class of $k$-degenerate graphs. Let $f_k(H)$ be the separation parameter defined by taking $f_k(H)=1$ when $H$ has no $(\leqslant k)$-separation, and otherwise taking the maximum number of pairwise independent $(\leqslant k)$-separations in $H$.

**Degenerate-graph density conjecture.** For every fixed $k$-degenerate graph $H$,

$$
C(H,\mathcal{D}_k,n) \in \Theta\left(n^{f_k(H)}\right).
$$

This is proposed as a generalisation of the paper's bounds for degenerate graph classes. The source does not report a proof or disproof, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: The improved ball-number bound for links
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a link. Its **ball number** $\mathsf{ball}(L)$ is the minimum number of non-overlapping solid balls needed in a necklace representation of $L$, and its **crossing number** $\mathsf{cr}(L)$ is the minimum crossing number among diagrams of $L$.

**Improved ball-number conjecture.** For every link $L$,

$$
\mathsf{ball}(L)\leq 4\mathsf{cr}(L).
$$

Moreover, equality holds if $L$ is alternating.

The paper proves the weaker upper bound $\mathsf{ball}(L)\leq 5\mathsf{cr}(L)$ and presents an explicit construction of necklace representations. The proposed improvement to $4\mathsf{cr}(L)$, together with the alternating-link equality statement, is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Jorge Luis Ramírez Alfonsín and Ivan Rasskin, “Ball packings for links”, arXiv:2010.00580 (2021).
record.references:

record.title: The aging conjecture for the running maximum of the Mott random walk
record.statement:
Let $\rho<1$, let $\beta,\lambda\geq0$, and let $Z^{\beta,\lambda}$ be the limiting process. For $h>1$, define

$$
\theta(h):=\mathbb{P}\left(\sup_{s\leq1}Z^{\beta,\lambda}_s=\sup_{s\leq h}Z^{\beta,\lambda}_s\right).
$$

**Aging conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}^{\beta,\lambda/n}\left(\sup_{s\leq n^{1+1/\rho}}X_s=\sup_{s\leq n^{1+1/\rho}h}X_s\right)=\theta(h)\qquad\text{for every }h>1,
$$

with

$$
\lim_{h\to1}\theta(h)=1,\qquad \lim_{h\to\infty}\theta(h)=0.
$$

This predicts aging of the running maximum: on the anomalous time scale, the maximum over a time interval remains unchanged when the observation interval is enlarged by a factor $h$ with probability tending to $\theta(h)$. The source presents this as an expected property and does not establish it.
record.source_name: David A. Croydon, Ryoki Fukushima and Stefan Junk, “Anomalous scaling regime for one-dimensional Mott variable-range hopping”, arXiv:2010.01779 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.01779

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

record.title: NP-hardness conjecture for promise CSPs between $\mathbf{LO}_k$ and $\mathbf{LO}_l$
record.statement: For integers $2\leq k<l$, let $\mathbf{LO}_k$ and $\mathbf{LO}_l$ denote the corresponding symmetric relational templates, and let $\mathrm{PCSP}(\mathbf{LO}_k,\mathbf{LO}_l)$ be the promise problem whose instances homomorphically map to $\mathbf{LO}_k$ and whose outputs must homomorphically map to $\mathbf{LO}_l$. **$\mathbf{LO}$-template hardness conjecture.** For every $2\leq k<l$, $\mathrm{PCSP}(\mathbf{LO}_k,\mathbf{LO}_l)$ is NP-hard. The paper has classified the relevant three-element cases except for $\mathbf{LO}_3$; the smallest case $\mathrm{PCSP}(\mathbf{LO}_2,\mathbf{LO}_3)$ is therefore among the unresolved instances motivating the conjecture.
record.source_name: Libor Barto, Diego Battistelli and Kevin M. Berg, “Symmetric Promise Constraint Satisfaction Problems: Beyond the Boolean Case”, arXiv:2010.04623 (2020).

record.title: The square-root error conjecture for optimal partial-feedback card guessing
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}^+$ denote the maximum expected number of correctly guessed cards in the partial-feedback card-guessing model with $m$ card types and $n$ copies of each type. **Square-root error conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ and $n$ sufficiently large,

$$
\mathcal{P}_{m,n}^+=m+O(m^{1/2+\varepsilon}).
$$

The conjecture would improve the paper's proved upper bound $m+O(m^{3/4}\log m)$ and would nearly match the known lower bound $m+\Omega(m^{1/2})$. The authors identify two parts of the proof where the current error term is oversized, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Persi Diaconis, Ron Graham, Xiaoyu He and Sam Spiro, “Card Guessing with Partial Feedback”, arXiv:2010.05059 (2022).

record.title: Post-first-step monotonicity conjecture for majority dynamics
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be a random graph sampled independently of an arbitrary initial red-blue coloring of its vertices, and let $\varepsilon>0$. Assume

$$
p\geq \frac{(1+\varepsilon)\log n}{n}.
$$

After the first step of majority dynamics, compare the numbers of vertices of the two colors. **Post-first-step monotonicity conjecture.** With probability tending to $1$, whichever color is more numerous after the first step will have increasingly more vertices after every subsequent step, until all vertices have that color. This stronger conjecture would, together with the paper's central limit theorem, determine the value of $\varepsilon$ in the one-extra-vertex conjecture.
record.source_name: Ross Berkowitz and Pat Devlin, “Central Limit Theorem for Majority Dynamics: Bribing Three Voters Suffices”, arXiv:2010.08172 (2020).

record.title: Eventual uniqueness of maximum independent sets in monomial graphs
record.statement:
For positive integers $n$ and nonnegative integers $d$, let $G_n(d)$ be the graph whose vertices are the monomials of degree $d$ in $n$ variables, with two monomials adjacent exactly when their least common multiple has degree $d+1$. Let $\mathbf{a}_n(d)$ denote the number of maximum independent sets of $G_n(d)$. **Eventual uniqueness conjecture.** For any $n \geq 1$, there exists some $N \geq 0$ such that $\mathbf{a}_n(d)=1$ whenever $d\equiv 0\pmod n$ and $d\geq N$.

The conjecture extends the paper's established uniqueness results in selected cases, particularly for $n=3$ with $d$ divisible by $3$ and for $n=4$ with $d$ even. It predicts eventual uniqueness along the multiples of the number of variables for every $n$.
record.source_name: John Machacek, “Unique maximum independent sets in graphs on monomials of a fixed degree”, arXiv:2010.11112 (2021).

record.title: The entropy-density conjecture for multigraph product extremal numbers
record.statement:
Let $a,r,s,d$ be integers with $a,r\geq 1$, $d\in[0,a-1]$, and $s\geq (r-1)(d+1)+2$. For sufficiently large $n$, write $\mathrm{ex}_{\Pi}(n,s,q)$ for the maximum edge-product among $(n,s,q)$-graphs, let $\Sigma_{r,d}(a,s)$ be the relevant maximum number of edges in an $s$-vertex set, and let $\Pi_{r,d}(a,n)$ denote the product supplied by the construction $\mathcal{T}_{r,d}(a,n)$. **Entropy-density conjecture.** For all such parameters and all sufficiently large $n$, 

$$
\mathrm{ex}_{\Pi}(n,s,\Sigma_{r,d}(a,s))=\Pi_{r,d}(a,n).
$$

Roughly, this says that the multigraph from $\mathcal{T}_{r,d}(a,n)$ maximises the edge-product subject to the prescribed local edge bound. The paper proves the $d=0$ case, while the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: A. Nicholas Day, Victor Falgas-Ravry and Andrew Treglown, “Extremal problems for multigraphs”, arXiv:2011.01626 (2021).

record.title: Four-line generation conjecture for line-arrangement ideals
record.statement:
Let $L=(\mathcal{P},\mathcal{L},\mathcal{I})$ be a line arrangement on $[n]$, and let $I_L$ and $G_L$ be the line-arrangement ideal and the collection of polynomials defined in the paper. If $L$ has at most four lines, then

**Four-line generation conjecture.**

$$
I_L=\langle G_L\rangle.
$$

The claim is supported by the line arrangements that the authors were able to compute, but the supplied text does not report a proof or a resolution for all line arrangements with at most four lines.
record.source_name: Oliver Clarke, Fatemeh Mohammadi and Harshit J. Motwani, “Conditional probabilities via line arrangements and point configurations”, arXiv:2011.02450 (2021).

record.title: Arithmetic pattern conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $N$ be positive integers. A $k$-term arithmetic progression has a basepoint $x$ and a common difference. Let $G_k(N)$ be the size of the smallest set of integers containing such a progression with basepoint $x$ for every $x\in[N]$, and let $G'_k(N)$ be the analogous minimum when the basepoints are $N$ distinct integer values. **Arithmetic pattern conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log G_k(N)}{\log N}=1
$$

and

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log G'_k(N)}{\log N}=1.
$$

This is presented as the type-(a) dual of the arithmetic Kakeya problem and is stated to be equivalent to the arithmetic Kakeya conjecture. The source gives no resolution of either formulation.
record.source_name: Charlie Cowen-Breen, Elene Karangozishvili, Narmada Varadarajan and Thomas Wang, “Pattern Problems related to the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture”, arXiv:2011.07056 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.07056

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

record.title: The $(U_k)$-pattern conjecture
record.statement:
Let $(U_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an increasing chain of subsets of $\mathbb{Q}^+$ with $|U_k|=k$. A $U_k$-pattern is a set obtained from $U_k$ by a common scaling and translation; $G'_{U_k}(N)$ denotes the size of the smallest set of integers containing a $U_k$-pattern with basepoint $x$ for $N$ distinct integer values of $x$. **The $(U_k)$-pattern conjecture.** For every such increasing chain,

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log G'_{U_k}(N)}{\log N}=1.
$$

This is technically a family of conjectures, one for each chain $(U_k)$. The source notes that integer and rational basepoints give the same quantity after clearing denominators.
record.source_name: Charlie Cowen-Breen, Elene Karangozishvili, Narmada Varadarajan and Thomas Wang, “Pattern Problems related to the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture”, arXiv:2011.07056 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: The restricted $(U_k)$-pattern conjecture
record.statement:
Let $(U_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an increasing chain of subsets of $\mathbb{N}^+$ with $|U_k|=k$. Let $G_{U_k}(N)$ be the size of the smallest set of integers containing a $U_k$-pattern with basepoint $x$ for every $x\in[N]$. **The restricted $(U_k)$-pattern conjecture.** For every such chain,

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log G_{U_k}(N)}{\log N}=1.
$$

The source states that, for chains contained in $\mathbb{N}^+$, this restricted conjecture is equivalent to the preceding pattern conjecture and hence to the relevant arithmetic Kakeya formulation. No resolution is given.
record.source_name: Charlie Cowen-Breen, Elene Karangozishvili, Narmada Varadarajan and Thomas Wang, “Pattern Problems related to the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture”, arXiv:2011.07056 (2020).

record.title: The $n$-dimensional finite-field $(U_k)$-pattern conjecture
record.statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and let $\pi_p:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{F}_p$ be the canonical projection. For $U\subset\mathbb{Z}$, a $U$-pattern in $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ is a set of the form $x+\pi_p(U)\cdot r$ with $x,r\in\mathbb{F}_p^n$ and $r\ne0$. Let $(U_k)$ be a sequence with $|U_k|=k$, and let $g_{n,U_k}(p)$ be the size of the smallest set containing a $U_k$-pattern with basepoint $x$ for every $x\in\mathbb{F}_p^n$. **The $n$-dimensional finite-field $(U_k)$-pattern conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{\log g_{n,U_k}(p)}{\log p}=n.
$$

This is technically a family indexed by $n$ and by the sequence $(U_k)$. The supplied text does not state any resolution or further consequences.
record.source_name: Charlie Cowen-Breen, Elene Karangozishvili, Narmada Varadarajan and Thomas Wang, “Pattern Problems related to the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture”, arXiv:2011.07056 (2020).

record.title: Herscovici–Hester–Hurlbert Target Conjecture for graph pebbling
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $D$ be a target distribution on $G$. Write $|D|$ for the total demand, $\pi(G,D)$ for the smallest integer $m$ such that every configuration of $m$ pebbles is $D$-solvable, and $\pi_t(G)$ for the maximum $t$-fold pebbling number over all target vertices, where $t=|D|$. **Target Conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\pi(G,D)\leq \pi_{|D|}(G)
$$

for every target distribution $D$. The conjecture is known for trees, cycles, complete graphs, and cubes, and the general case remains open; it is intended as a tool for studying pebbling numbers more broadly, including chordal graphs and Cartesian products.
record.source_name: Glenn Hurlbert and Essak Seddiq, “On the Target Pebbling Conjecture”, arXiv:2011.10623 (2021).
record.references:
